why: With unlimited parallelism, a course finishes at its own duration plus the latest finish among its prerequisites: the longest weighted path in a DAG. Only the targets' prerequisite closure matters, and the answer is the largest finish time among the targets.
hints: If courses can run in parallel, what is the only thing that delays a course from starting?
finish[c] = durations[c] + max(finish[p]) over its prerequisites p. Compute it in topological order (or DFS with memo).
Collect the closure of the targets by walking prerequisites, run Kahn's algorithm on it computing finish times, and return the max over targets. Use integer arithmetic; sums reach 10^14. O(V + E).
pitfalls: Courses outside the targets' closure must not affect the answer.
